the_signal.headline: Event-driven microservices beat batch—async APIs now your GTM baseline
the_signal.body: n8n's breakdown shows event-driven architecture is winning over legacy async patterns for real-time customer workflows. GTM teams building on batch-heavy stacks are leaving 10-50ms of latency (and conversion rate) on the table. Your automation backbone needs to shift from scheduled jobs to stream-based event consumption now.

tool_drop.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (via n8n)
tool_drop.what: Single orchestration layer that runs multi-agent teams with persistent memory across specialist agents (compute, knowledge retrieval, investigation).
tool_drop.why: Solves the routing-and-recall problem in customer-facing AI systems—agents stop duplicating context lookups and start actually collaborating on triage at scale.

thread_of_day.title: RPA vs. Workflow Automation: Which Actually Ships in Production
thread_of_day.takeaway: RPA dies when you need observability and debugging; workflow automation with native async APIs wins because you can actually see what broke and why.

quote.text: Event-driven microservices eliminate polling and batch delays—your automation moves at the speed of data, not the speed of your scheduler.

whats_moving.context: As GTM teams embed more automation, poorly secured API integrations become liability vectors—token rotation and OAuth are no longer optional.
Enterprise GTM buyers are rejecting vendor lock-in; n8n alternatives comparison signals demand for deployable, code-extensible automation without SaaS constraints.
Traffic camera backdoors and Android head-unit malware remind GTM ops that infrastructure assumptions break—third-party device/firmware compromises now threaten customer data pipelines.

act_on_this: Audit your current GTM automation stack: identify batch jobs that should be event-driven and replace them. Start with your highest-volume customer touchpoint (lead routing, payment confirmation, onboarding trigger)—measure the latency delta.

numbers.stat: 3 specialist agents (compute, knowledge, investigation) running on a single orchestration layer in the Bedrock example
numbers.context: This is the baseline for production multi-agent GTM systems—anything less and you're losing coordination gains; anything more and debugging becomes impossible.
